title: Regular follow-up for a long-term illness
what: Regular visits to the doctor for a long-term illness. The doctor checks how treatment is going and keeps the illness from getting worse.
why: For high blood pressure, diabetes, heart, lung, or kidney disease, and other long-term illnesses.
duration: a visit usually takes 15 to 30 minutes, usually 1 to 4 times a year, as your doctor plans
tell_doctor: How you have felt since the last visit
Whether you take your medicines and how you tolerate them
Whether you had flare-ups, ambulance calls, or hospital stays

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Before the visit you often need to have tests. Check which ones and when.

prepare.title: Diary
prepare.text: Bring your blood pressure, sugar, or symptom records.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Take them as usual. Do not stop them on your own.

bring: A blood pressure or sugar diary
steps: The doctor asks how you feel
Measures blood pressure, weight, and other readings
Decides whether to keep or change the treatment
Sets the date of your next visit
feel: If blood is drawn, a short prick
after: Come on the set dates, even if you feel well
Write down questions for your next visit
Do not stop your medicines on your own
red_flags: A sudden worsening of your illness, severe chest pain, or shortness of breath: call emergency services

faq.q: Why go if I feel fine?
faq.a: This way the doctor notices a worsening before you feel it.

faq.q: Can I be taken off the follow-up list?
faq.a: Your doctor decides, usually if the illness is gone or has not shown up for a long time.

reminders.text: Routine doctor visit tomorrow. Bring your diary of readings and recent tests.
